# log - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/log/^0.4.22/

## Expand description

A lightweight logging facade.

The `log` crate provides a single logging API that abstracts over the
actual logging implementation. Libraries can use the logging API provided
by this crate, and the consumer of those libraries can choose the logging
implementation that is most suitable for its use case.

If no logging implementation is selected, the facade falls back to a “noop” implementation that ignores all log messages. The overhead in this case is very small - just an integer load, comparison and jump.

A log request consists of a *target*, a *level*, and a *body*. A target is a
string which defaults to the module path of the location of the log request,
though that default may be overridden. Logger implementations typically use
the target to filter requests based on some user configuration.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

The basic use of the log crate is through the five logging macros: [ error!](https://docs.rs/macro.error.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/macro.warn.html)

`warn!`[,](https://docs.rs/macro.info.html)

`info!`[and](https://docs.rs/macro.debug.html)

`debug!`[where](https://docs.rs/macro.trace.html)

`trace!``error!` represents the highest-priority log messages
and `trace!` the lowest. The log messages are filtered by configuring
the log level to exclude messages with a lower priority.
Each of these macros accept format strings similarly to [.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/macro.println.html)

`println!`Avoid writing expressions with side-effects in log statements. They may not be evaluated.

[§](https://docs.rs#in-libraries)In libraries

Libraries should link only to the `log` crate, and use the provided
macros to log whatever information will be useful to downstream consumers.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use log::{info, warn};
pub fn shave_the_yak(yak: &mut Yak) {
    info!(target: "yak_events", "Commencing yak shaving for {yak:?}");
    loop {
        match find_a_razor() {
            Ok(razor) => {
                info!("Razor located: {razor}");
                yak.shave(razor);
                break;
            }
            Err(err) => {
                warn!("Unable to locate a razor: {err}, retrying");
            }
        }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#in-executables)In executables

Executables should choose a logging implementation and initialize it early in the runtime of the program. Logging implementations will typically include a function to do this. Any log messages generated before the implementation is initialized will be ignored.

The executable itself may use the `log` crate to log as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#warning)Warning

The logging system may only be initialized once.

[§](https://docs.rs#structured-logging)Structured logging

If you enable the `kv` feature you can associate structured values
with your log records. If we take the example from before, we can include
some additional context besides what’s in the formatted message:

```
use log::{info, warn};
pub fn shave_the_yak(yak: &mut Yak) {
    info!(target: "yak_events", yak:serde; "Commencing yak shaving");
    loop {
        match find_a_razor() {
            Ok(razor) => {
                info!(razor; "Razor located");
                yak.shave(razor);
                break;
            }
            Err(e) => {
                warn!(e:err; "Unable to locate a razor, retrying");
            }
        }
    }
}
```
See the [ kv](https://docs.rs/kv/index.html) module documentation for more details.

[§](https://docs.rs#available-logging-implementations)Available logging implementations

In order to produce log output executables have to use a logger implementation compatible with the facade. There are many available implementations to choose from, here are some of the most popular ones:

- Simple minimal loggers:
- Complex configurable frameworks:
- Adaptors for other facilities:
- For WebAssembly binaries:
- For dynamic libraries:
- You may need to construct an FFI-safe wrapper over `log`to initialize in your libraries

- You may need to construct an FFI-safe wrapper over
- Utilities:

[§](https://docs.rs#implementing-a-logger)Implementing a Logger

Loggers implement the [ Log](https://docs.rs/trait.Log.html) trait. Here’s a very basic example that simply
logs all messages at the

[,](https://docs.rs/enum.Level.html)

`Error`[or](https://docs.rs/enum.Level.html)

`Warn`[levels to stdout:](https://docs.rs/enum.Level.html)

`Info````
use log::{Record, Level, Metadata};
struct SimpleLogger;
impl log::Log for SimpleLogger {
    fn enabled(&self, metadata: &Metadata) -> bool {
        metadata.level() <= Level::Info
    }
    fn log(&self, record: &Record) {
        if self.enabled(record.metadata()) {
            println!("{} - {}", record.level(), record.args());
        }
    }
    fn flush(&self) {}
}
```
Loggers are installed by calling the [ set_logger](https://docs.rs/fn.set_logger.html) function. The maximum
log level also needs to be adjusted via the

[function. The logging facade uses this as an optimization to improve performance of log messages at levels that are disabled. It’s important to set it, as it defaults to](https://docs.rs/fn.set_max_level.html)

`set_max_level`[, so no log messages will ever be captured! In the case of our example logger, we’ll want to set the maximum log level to](https://docs.rs/enum.LevelFilter.html)

`Off`[, since we ignore any](https://docs.rs/enum.LevelFilter.html)

`Info`[or](https://docs.rs/enum.Level.html)

`Debug`[level log messages. A logging implementation should provide a function that wraps a call to](https://docs.rs/enum.Level.html)

`Trace`[and](https://docs.rs/fn.set_logger.html)

`set_logger`[, handling initialization of the logger:](https://docs.rs/fn.set_max_level.html)

`set_max_level````
use log::{SetLoggerError, LevelFilter};
static LOGGER: SimpleLogger = SimpleLogger;
pub fn init() -> Result<(), SetLoggerError> {
    log::set_logger(&LOGGER)
        .map(|()| log::set_max_level(LevelFilter::Info))
}
```
Implementations that adjust their configurations at runtime should take care to adjust the maximum log level as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#use-with-std)Use with `std`

`set_logger` requires you to provide a `&'static Log`, which can be hard to
obtain if your logger depends on some runtime configuration. The
`set_boxed_logger` function is available with the `std` Cargo feature. It is
identical to `set_logger` except that it takes a `Box<Log>` rather than a
`&'static Log`:

```
pub fn init() -> Result<(), SetLoggerError> {
    log::set_boxed_logger(Box::new(SimpleLogger))
        .map(|()| log::set_max_level(LevelFilter::Info))
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#compile-time-filters)Compile time filters

Log levels can be statically disabled at compile time by enabling one of these Cargo features:

- `max_level_off`
- `max_level_error`
- `max_level_warn`
- `max_level_info`
- `max_level_debug`
- `max_level_trace`

Log invocations at disabled levels will be skipped and will not even be present in the
resulting binary. These features control the value of the `STATIC_MAX_LEVEL` constant. The
logging macros check this value before logging a message. By default, no levels are disabled.

It is possible to override this level for release builds only with the following features:

- `release_max_level_off`
- `release_max_level_error`
- `release_max_level_warn`
- `release_max_level_info`
- `release_max_level_debug`
- `release_max_level_trace`

Libraries should avoid using the max level features because they’re global and can’t be changed once they’re set.

For example, a crate can disable trace level logs in debug builds and trace, debug, and info level logs in release builds with the following configuration:

```
[dependencies]
log = { version = "0.4", features = ["max_level_debug", "release_max_level_warn"] }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#crate-feature-flags)Crate Feature Flags

The following crate feature flags are available in addition to the filters. They are
configured in your `Cargo.toml`.

- `std`allows use of- `std`crate instead of the default- `core`. Enables using- `std::error`and- `set_boxed_logger`functionality.
- `serde`enables support for serialization and deserialization of- `Level`and- `LevelFilter`.

```
[dependencies]
log = { version = "0.4", features = ["std", "serde"] }
```
[§](https://docs.rs#version-compatibility)Version compatibility

The 0.3 and 0.4 versions of the `log` crate are almost entirely compatible. Log messages
made using `log` 0.3 will forward transparently to a logger implementation using `log` 0.4. Log
messages made using `log` 0.4 will forward to a logger implementation using `log` 0.3, but the
module path and file name information associated with the message will unfortunately be lost.

# serde - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde/^1.0.214/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#serde)Serde

Serde is a framework for * ser*ializing and

*serializing Rust data structures efficiently and generically.*

**de**The Serde ecosystem consists of data structures that know how to serialize and deserialize themselves along with data formats that know how to serialize and deserialize other things. Serde provides the layer by which these two groups interact with each other, allowing any supported data structure to be serialized and deserialized using any supported data format.

See the Serde website [https://serde.rs](https://serde.rs) for additional documentation and
usage examples.

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

Where many other languages rely on runtime reflection for serializing data,
Serde is instead built on Rust’s powerful trait system. A data structure
that knows how to serialize and deserialize itself is one that implements
Serde’s `Serialize` and `Deserialize` traits (or uses Serde’s derive
attribute to automatically generate implementations at compile time). This
avoids any overhead of reflection or runtime type information. In fact in
many situations the interaction between data structure and data format can
be completely optimized away by the Rust compiler, leaving Serde
serialization to perform the same speed as a handwritten serializer for the
specific selection of data structure and data format.

[§](https://docs.rs#data-formats)Data formats

The following is a partial list of data formats that have been implemented for Serde by the community.

- [JSON](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), the ubiquitous JavaScript Object Notation used by many HTTP APIs.
- [Postcard](https://github.com/jamesmunns/postcard), a no_std and embedded-systems friendly compact binary format.
- [CBOR](https://github.com/enarx/ciborium), a Concise Binary Object Representation designed for small message size without the need for version negotiation.
- [YAML](https://github.com/dtolnay/serde-yaml), a self-proclaimed human-friendly configuration language that ain’t markup language.
- [MessagePack](https://github.com/3Hren/msgpack-rust), an efficient binary format that resembles a compact JSON.
- [TOML](https://docs.rs/toml), a minimal configuration format used by- [Cargo](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html).
- [Pickle](https://github.com/birkenfeld/serde-pickle), a format common in the Python world.
- [RON](https://github.com/ron-rs/ron), a Rusty Object Notation.
- [BSON](https://github.com/mongodb/bson-rust), the data storage and network transfer format used by MongoDB.
- [Avro](https://docs.rs/apache-avro), a binary format used within Apache Hadoop, with support for schema definition.
- [JSON5](https://github.com/callum-oakley/json5-rs), a superset of JSON including some productions from ES5.
- [URL](https://docs.rs/serde_qs)query strings, in the x-www-form-urlencoded format.
- [Starlark](https://github.com/dtolnay/serde-starlark), the format used for describing build targets by the Bazel and Buck build systems.- *(serialization only)*
- [Envy](https://github.com/softprops/envy), a way to deserialize environment variables into Rust structs.- *(deserialization only)*
- [Envy Store](https://github.com/softprops/envy-store), a way to deserialize- [AWS Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html)parameters into Rust structs.- *(deserialization only)*
- [S-expressions](https://github.com/rotty/lexpr-rs), the textual representation of code and data used by the Lisp language family.
- [D-Bus](https://docs.rs/zvariant)’s binary wire format.
- [FlexBuffers](https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/tree/master/rust/flexbuffers), the schemaless cousin of Google’s FlatBuffers zero-copy serialization format.
- [Bencode](https://github.com/P3KI/bendy), a simple binary format used in the BitTorrent protocol.
- [Token streams](https://github.com/oxidecomputer/serde_tokenstream), for processing Rust procedural macro input.- *(deserialization only)*
- [DynamoDB Items](https://docs.rs/serde_dynamo), the format used by- [rusoto_dynamodb](https://docs.rs/rusoto_dynamodb)to transfer data to and from DynamoDB.
- [Hjson](https://github.com/Canop/deser-hjson), a syntax extension to JSON designed around human reading and editing.- *(deserialization only)*
- [CSV](https://docs.rs/csv), Comma-separated values is a tabular text file format.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [de](https://docs.rs/de/index.html)
- Generic data structure deserialization framework.
- [ser](https://docs.rs/ser/index.html)
- Generic data structure serialization framework.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [forward_](https://docs.rs/macro.forward_to_deserialize_any.html)- to_ - deserialize_ - any - `docsrs`
- Helper macro when implementing the `Deserializer`part of a new data format for Serde.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be deserialized from any data format supported by Serde.
- [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserializer.html)
- A **data format**that can deserialize any data structure supported by Serde.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Serialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be serialized into any data format supported by Serde.
- [Serializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Serializer.html)
- A **data format**that can serialize any data structure supported by Serde.

- Derive macro available if serde is built with `features = ["derive"]`.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/derive.Serialize.html)- `derive`
- Derive macro available if serde is built with `features = ["derive"]`.

# sp_runtime - Rust

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#substrate-runtime-primitives)Substrate Runtime Primitives.

This crate, among other things, contains a large library of types and utilities that are used in
the Substrate runtime, but are not particularly `FRAME`-oriented.

[§](https://docs.rs#block-header-and-extrinsics)Block, Header and Extrinsics

Most notable, this crate contains some of the types and trait that enable important communication between the client and the runtime. This includes:

- A set of traits to declare what any block/header/extrinsic type should provide.
- A set of types that implement these traits, whilst still providing a high degree of configurability via generics.

[§](https://docs.rs#runtime-api-types)Runtime API Types

This crate also contains some types that are often used in conjuncture with Runtime APIs. Most notable:

- `ApplyExtrinsicResult`- `DispatchOutcome`
- `transaction_validity`

# criterion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/criterion/^0.5.1/

## Expand description

A statistics-driven micro-benchmarking library written in Rust.

This crate is a microbenchmarking library which aims to provide strong statistical confidence in detecting and estimating the size of performance improvements and regressions, while also being easy to use.

See
[the user guide](https://bheisler.github.io/criterion.rs/book/index.html)
for examples as well as details on the measurement and analysis process,
and the output.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features:

- Collects detailed statistics, providing strong confidence that changes to performance are real, not measurement noise.
- Produces detailed charts, providing thorough understanding of your code’s performance behavior.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [async_](https://docs.rs/async_executor/index.html)- executor
- This module defines a trait that can be used to plug in different Futures executors into Criterion.rs’ async benchmarking support.
- [measurement](https://docs.rs/measurement/index.html)
- This module defines a set of traits that can be used to plug different measurements (eg.
Unix’s Processor Time, CPU or GPU performance counters, etc.) into Criterion.rs. It also
includes the [WallTime](https://docs.rs/struct.WallTime.html)struct which defines the default wall-clock time measurement.
- [profiler](https://docs.rs/profiler/index.html)
- This module provides an extension trait which allows in-process profilers
to be hooked into the `--profile-time`argument at compile-time. Users of out-of-process profilers such as perf don’t need to do anything special.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [criterion_](https://docs.rs/macro.criterion_group.html)- group
- Macro used to define a function group for the benchmark harness; see the
`criterion_main!`macro for more details.
- [criterion_](https://docs.rs/macro.criterion_main.html)- main
- Macro which expands to a benchmark harness.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Async](https://docs.rs/struct.AsyncBencher.html)- Bencher
- Async/await variant of the Bencher struct.
- [Bencher](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html)
- Timer struct used to iterate a benchmarked function and measure the runtime.
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/struct.BenchmarkGroup.html)- Group
- Structure used to group together a set of related benchmarks, along with custom configuration settings for groups of benchmarks. All benchmarks performed using a benchmark group will be grouped together in the final report.
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/struct.BenchmarkId.html)- Id
- Simple structure representing an ID for a benchmark. The ID must be unique within a benchmark group.
- [Criterion](https://docs.rs/struct.Criterion.html)
- The benchmark manager
- [Plot](https://docs.rs/struct.PlotConfiguration.html)- Configuration
- Contains the configuration options for the plots generated by a particular benchmark or benchmark group.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Axis](https://docs.rs/enum.AxisScale.html)- Scale
- Axis scaling type
- [Baseline](https://docs.rs/enum.Baseline.html)
- Baseline describes how the baseline_directory is handled.
- [Batch](https://docs.rs/enum.BatchSize.html)- Size
- Argument to `Bencher::iter_batched``Bencher::iter_batched_ref`
- [Benchmark](https://docs.rs/enum.BenchmarkFilter.html)- Filter
- Benchmark filtering support.
- [Plotting](https://docs.rs/enum.PlottingBackend.html)- Backend
- Enum used to select the plotting backend.
- [Sampling](https://docs.rs/enum.SamplingMode.html)- Mode
- This enum allows the user to control how Criterion.rs chooses the iteration count when sampling. The default is Auto, which will choose a method automatically based on the iteration time during the warm-up phase.
- [Throughput](https://docs.rs/enum.Throughput.html)
- Enum representing different ways of measuring the throughput of benchmarked code. If the throughput setting is configured for a benchmark then the estimated throughput will be reported as well as the time per iteration.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [black_](https://docs.rs/fn.black_box.html)- box
- A function that is opaque to the optimizer, used to prevent the compiler from optimizing away computations in a benchmark.

# frame_system - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/frame-system/48.0.0/target-redirect/frame_system/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#system-pallet)System Pallet

The System pallet provides low-level access to core types and cross-cutting utilities. It acts as the base layer for other pallets to interact with the Substrate framework components.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

The System pallet defines the core data types used in a Substrate runtime. It also provides
several utility functions (see [ Pallet](https://docs.rs/pallet/struct.Pallet.html)) for other FRAME pallets.

In addition, it manages the storage items for extrinsic data, indices, event records, and digest items, among other things that support the execution of the current block.

It also handles low-level tasks like depositing logs, basic set up and take down of temporary storage entries, and access to previous block hashes.

[§](https://docs.rs#interface)Interface

[§](https://docs.rs#dispatchable-functions)Dispatchable Functions

The System pallet provides dispatchable functions that, with the exception of `remark`, manage
low-level or privileged functionality of a Substrate-based runtime.

- `remark`: Make some on-chain remark.
- `set_heap_pages`: Set the number of pages in the WebAssembly environment’s heap.
- `set_code`: Set the new runtime code.
- `set_code_without_checks`: Set the new runtime code without any checks.
- `set_storage`: Set some items of storage.
- `kill_storage`: Kill some items from storage.
- `kill_prefix`: Kill all storage items with a key that starts with the given prefix.
- `remark_with_event`: Make some on-chain remark and emit an event.
- `do_task`: Do some specified task.
- `authorize_upgrade`: Authorize new runtime code.
- `authorize_upgrade_without_checks`: Authorize new runtime code and an upgrade sans verification.
- `apply_authorized_upgrade`: Provide new, already-authorized runtime code.

[§](https://docs.rs#a-note-on-upgrades)A Note on Upgrades

The pallet provides two primary means of upgrading the runtime, a single-phase means using
`set_code` and a two-phase means using `authorize_upgrade` followed by
`apply_authorized_upgrade`. The first will directly attempt to apply the provided `code`
(application may have to be scheduled, depending on the context and implementation of the
`OnSetCode` trait).

The `authorize_upgrade` route allows the authorization of a runtime’s code hash. Once
authorized, anyone may upload the correct runtime to apply the code. This pattern is useful when
providing the runtime ahead of time may be unwieldy, for example when a large preimage (the
code) would need to be stored on-chain or sent over a message transport protocol such as a
bridge.

The `*_without_checks` variants do not perform any version checks, so using them runs the risk
of applying a downgrade or entirely other chain specification. They will still validate that the
`code` meets the authorized hash.

[§](https://docs.rs#public-functions)Public Functions

See the [ Pallet](https://docs.rs/pallet/struct.Pallet.html) struct for details of publicly available functions.

[§](https://docs.rs#signed-extensions)Signed Extensions

The System pallet defines the following extensions:

- `CheckWeight`
- `CheckNonce`- `T::Nonce`.
- `CheckEra`- `Era`.
- `CheckGenesis`
- `CheckSpecVersion`
- `CheckTxVersion`

Look up the runtime aggregator file (e.g. `node/runtime`) to see the full list of signed
extensions included in a chain.

[§](https://docs.rs#public-functions)Public Functions

See the [ Pallet](https://docs.rs/pallet/struct.Pallet.html) struct for details of publicly available functions.

[§](https://docs.rs#signed-extensions)Signed Extensions

The System pallet defines the following extensions:

- `CheckWeight`
- `CheckNonce`- `T::Nonce`.
- `CheckEra`- `Era`.
- `CheckGenesis`
- `CheckSpecVersion`
- `CheckTxVersion`

Look up the runtime aggregator file (e.g. `node/runtime`) to see the full list of signed
extensions included in a chain.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use weights::`- [WeightInfo](https://docs.rs/weights/trait.WeightInfo.html);
- `pub use`- [pallet](https://docs.rs/pallet/index.html)::*;

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [limits](https://docs.rs/limits/index.html)
- Block resource limits configuration structures.
- [migrations](https://docs.rs/migrations/index.html)
- Migrate the reference counting state.
- [mocking](https://docs.rs/mocking/index.html)
- Provide types to help defining a mock environment when testing pallets.
- [offchain](https://docs.rs/offchain/index.html)
- Module helpers for off-chain calls.
- [pallet](https://docs.rs/pallet/index.html)
- The `pallet`module in each FRAME pallet hosts the most important items needed to construct this pallet.
- [pallet_](https://docs.rs/pallet_prelude/index.html)- prelude
- Prelude to be used alongside pallet macro, for ease of use.
- [weights](https://docs.rs/weights/index.html)
- Autogenerated weights for `frame_system`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Account](https://docs.rs/struct.AccountInfo.html)- Info
- Information of an account.
- [Authorize](https://docs.rs/struct.AuthorizeCall.html)- Call
- A transaction extension that authorizes some calls (i.e. dispatchable functions) to be included in the block.
- [Chain](https://docs.rs/struct.ChainContext.html)- Context
- [Check](https://docs.rs/struct.CheckEra.html)- Era
- Check for transaction mortality.
- [Check](https://docs.rs/struct.CheckGenesis.html)- Genesis
- Genesis hash check to provide replay protection between different networks.
- [Check](https://docs.rs/struct.CheckMortality.html)- Mortality
- Check for transaction mortality.
- [Check](https://docs.rs/struct.CheckNonZeroSender.html)- NonZero - Sender
- Check to ensure that the sender is not the zero address.
- [Check](https://docs.rs/struct.CheckNonce.html)- Nonce
- Nonce check and increment to give replay protection for transactions.
- [Check](https://docs.rs/struct.CheckSpecVersion.html)- Spec - Version
- Ensure the runtime version registered in the transaction is the same as at present.
- [Check](https://docs.rs/struct.CheckTxVersion.html)- TxVersion
- Ensure the transaction version registered in the transaction is the same as at present.
- [Check](https://docs.rs/struct.CheckWeight.html)- Weight
- Block resource (weight) limit check.
- [Code](https://docs.rs/struct.CodeUpgradeAuthorization.html)- Upgrade - Authorization
- Information needed when a new runtime binary is submitted and needs to be authorized before replacing the current runtime.
- [Consumer](https://docs.rs/struct.Consumer.html)
- Event handler which registers a consumer when created.
- [Dispatch](https://docs.rs/struct.DispatchEventInfo.html)- Event - Info
- Information about the dispatch of a call, to be displayed in the
`ExtrinsicSuccess``ExtrinsicFailed`
- [Ensure](https://docs.rs/struct.EnsureNever.html)- Never
- Always fail.
- [Ensure](https://docs.rs/struct.EnsureNone.html)- None
- Ensure the origin is `None`. i.e. unsigned transaction.
- [Ensure](https://docs.rs/struct.EnsureRoot.html)- Root
- Ensure the origin is Root.
- [Ensure](https://docs.rs/struct.EnsureRootWithSuccess.html)- Root - With - Success
- Ensure the origin is Root and return the provided `Success`value.
- [Ensure](https://docs.rs/struct.EnsureSigned.html)- Signed
- Ensure the origin is any `Signed`origin.
- [Ensure](https://docs.rs/struct.EnsureSignedBy.html)- Signed - By
- Ensure the origin is `Signed`origin from the given`AccountId`.
- [Ensure](https://docs.rs/struct.EnsureWithSuccess.html)- With - Success
- Ensure the origin is provided `Ensure`origin and return the provided`Success`value.
- [Event](https://docs.rs/struct.EventRecord.html)- Record
- Record of an event happening.
- [Last](https://docs.rs/struct.LastRuntimeUpgradeInfo.html)- Runtime - Upgrade - Info
- Stores the `spec_version`and`spec_name`of when the last runtime upgrade happened.
- [Provider](https://docs.rs/struct.Provider.html)
- Event handler which registers a provider when created.
- [RunTo](https://docs.rs/struct.RunToBlockHooks.html)- Block - Hooks
- Hooks for the `Pallet::run_to_block_with`
- [Self](https://docs.rs/struct.SelfSufficient.html)- Sufficient
- Event handler which registers a self-sufficient when created.
- [Substrate](https://docs.rs/struct.SubstrateExtensionsWeight.html)- Extensions - Weight
- Weights for `frame_system_extensions`using the Substrate node and recommended hardware.
- [Valid](https://docs.rs/struct.ValidNonceInfo.html)- Nonce - Info
- For a valid transaction the provides and requires information related to the nonce.
- [Weight](https://docs.rs/struct.WeightReclaim.html)- Reclaim
- Reclaim the unused weight using the post dispatch information

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [calculate_](https://docs.rs/fn.calculate_consumed_extrinsic_weight.html)- consumed_ - extrinsic_ - weight
- Returns the weight that `CheckWeight`books for an extrinsic before dispatch.
- [ensure_](https://docs.rs/fn.ensure_authorized.html)- authorized
- Ensure that the origin `o`represents an extrinsic with authorized call. Returns`Ok`or an`Err`otherwise.
- [ensure_](https://docs.rs/fn.ensure_none.html)- none
- Ensure that the origin `o`represents an unsigned extrinsic. Returns`Ok`or an`Err`otherwise.
- [ensure_](https://docs.rs/fn.ensure_root.html)- root
- Ensure that the origin `o`represents the root. Returns`Ok`or an`Err`otherwise.
- [ensure_](https://docs.rs/fn.ensure_signed.html)- signed
- Ensure that the origin `o`represents a signed extrinsic (i.e. transaction). Returns`Ok`with the account that signed the extrinsic or an`Err`otherwise.
- [ensure_](https://docs.rs/fn.ensure_signed_or_root.html)- signed_ - or_ - root
- Ensure that the origin `o`represents either a signed extrinsic (i.e. transaction) or the root. Returns`Ok`with the account that signed the extrinsic,`None`if it was root, or an`Err`otherwise.
- [extrinsics_](https://docs.rs/fn.extrinsics_data_root.html)- data_ - root
- Compute the trie root of a list of extrinsics.
- [extrinsics_](https://docs.rs/fn.extrinsics_root.html)- root
- Compute the trie root of a list of extrinsics.
- [split_](https://docs.rs/fn.split_inner.html)- inner
- Split an `option`into two constituent options, as defined by a`splitter`function.
- [unique](https://docs.rs/fn.unique.html)
- Returns a 32 byte datum which is guaranteed to be universally unique. `entropy`is provided as a facility to reduce the potential for precalculating results.

[875](#875)			code: Vec<u8>,
[876](#876)		) -> DispatchResultWithPostInfo {
[877](#877)			let res = Self::validate_code_is_authorized(&code)?;
[878](#878)			AuthorizedUpgrade::<T>::kill();
[879](#879)
[880](#880)			match Self::can_set_code(&code, res.check_version) {
[881](#881)				CanSetCodeResult::Ok => {},
[882](#882)				CanSetCodeResult::MultiBlockMigrationsOngoing => {
[883](#883)					return Err(Error::<T>::MultiBlockMigrationsOngoing.into())
[884](#884)				},
[885](#885)				CanSetCodeResult::InvalidVersion(error) => {
[886](#886)					Self::deposit_event(Event::RejectedInvalidAuthorizedUpgrade {
[888](#888)						code_hash: res.code_hash,
[889](#889)						error: error.into(),
[890](#890)					});
[891](#891)
[892](#892)					return Ok(Pays::No.into());
[894](#894)				},
[895](#895)			};
[896](#896)			T::OnSetCode::set_code(code)?;
[897](#897)
[898](#898)			Ok(PostDispatchInfo {
[899](#899)				actual_weight: Some(T::BlockWeights::get().max_block),
[901](#901)				pays_fee: Pays::No,
[903](#903)			})
[904](#904)		}
[905](#905)	}

Authorize an upgrade to a given `code_hash` for the runtime. The runtime can be supplied
later.

WARNING: This authorizes an upgrade that will take place without any safety checks, for
example that the spec name remains the same and that the version number increases. Not
recommended for normal use. Use `authorize_upgrade` instead.

This call requires Root origin.

Provide the preimage (runtime binary) `code` for an upgrade that has been authorized.

If the authorization required a version check, this call will ensure the spec name remains unchanged and that the spec version has increased.

Depending on the runtime’s `OnSetCode` configuration, this function may directly apply
the new `code` in the same block or attempt to schedule the upgrade.

All origins are allowed.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/frame_system/lib.rs.html#1580-1582)#### pub fn [last_runtime_upgrade_spec_version](https://docs.rs#method.last_runtime_upgrade_spec_version)() -> [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/frame_system/lib.rs.html#1580-1582)

#### pub fn [last_runtime_upgrade_spec_version](https://docs.rs#method.last_runtime_upgrade_spec_version)() -> [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)

Returns the `spec_version` of the last runtime upgrade.

This function is useful for writing guarded runtime migrations in the runtime. A runtime
migration can use the `spec_version` to ensure that it isn’t applied twice. This works
similar as the storage version for pallets.

This functions returns the `spec_version` of the last runtime upgrade while executing the
runtime migrations
[ on_runtime_upgrade](https://docs.rs/frame-support/48.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/frame_support/traits/hooks/trait.OnRuntimeUpgrade.html#method.on_runtime_upgrade)
function. After all migrations are executed, this will return the

`spec_version` of the
current runtime until there is another runtime upgrade.Example:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[test]
fn last_runtime_upgrade_spec_version_usage() {
	#[allow(dead_code)]
	struct Migration;
	impl OnRuntimeUpgrade for Migration {
		fn on_runtime_upgrade() -> Weight {
			// Ensure to compare the spec version against some static version to prevent applying
			// the same migration multiple times.
			//
			// `1337` here is the spec version of the runtime running on chain. If there is maybe
			// a runtime upgrade in the pipeline of being applied, you should use the spec version
			// of this upgrade.
			if System::last_runtime_upgrade_spec_version() > 1337 {
				return Weight::zero();
			}
			// Do the migration.
			Weight::zero()
		}
	}
}
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/frame_system/lib.rs.html#1958-1962)#### pub fn [register_extra_weight_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.register_extra_weight_unchecked)(weight: [Weight](https://docs.rs/sp-weights/36.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sp_weights/weight_v2/struct.Weight.html), class: [DispatchClass](https://docs.rs/frame-support/48.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/frame_support/dispatch/enum.DispatchClass.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/frame_system/lib.rs.html#1958-1962)

#### pub fn [register_extra_weight_unchecked](https://docs.rs#method.register_extra_weight_unchecked)(weight: [Weight](https://docs.rs/sp-weights/36.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sp_weights/weight_v2/struct.Weight.html), class: [DispatchClass](https://docs.rs/frame-support/48.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/frame_support/dispatch/enum.DispatchClass.html))

Inform the system pallet of some additional weight that should be accounted for, in the current block.

NOTE: use with extra care; this function is made public only be used for certain pallets
that need it. A runtime that does not have dynamic calls should never need this and should
stick to static weights. A typical use case for this is inner calls or smart contract calls.
Furthermore, it only makes sense to use this when it is presumably  *cheap* to provide the
argument `weight`; In other words, if this function is to be used to account for some
unknown, user provided call’s weight, it would only make sense to use it if you are sure you
can rapidly compute the weight of the inner call.

Even more dangerous is to note that this function does NOT take any action, if the new sum
of block weight is more than the block weight limit. This is what the *unchecked*.

Another potential use-case could be for the `on_initialize` and `on_finalize` hooks.

# CheckNonce in frame_system - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/frame-system/48.0.0/frame_system/struct.CheckNonce.html

## Expand description

Nonce check and increment to give replay protection for transactions.

[§](https://docs.rs#transaction-validity)Transaction Validity

This extension affects `requires` and `provides` tags of validity, but DOES NOT
set the `priority` field. Make sure that AT LEAST one of the transaction extension sets
some kind of priority upon validating transactions.

The preparation step assumes that the nonce information has not changed since the validation
step. This means that other extensions ahead of `CheckNonce` in the pipeline must not alter the
nonce during their own preparation step, or else the transaction may be rejected during dispatch
or lead to an inconsistent account state.

## Tuple Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

# CheckMortality in frame_system - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/frame-system/48.0.0/frame_system/struct.CheckMortality.html

## Expand description

Check for transaction mortality.

The extension adds [ Era](https://docs.rs/sp-runtime/48.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sp_runtime/generic/era/enum.Era.html) to every signed extrinsic. It also contributes to the signed data, by
including the hash of the block at

[.](https://docs.rs/sp-runtime/48.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sp_runtime/generic/era/enum.Era.html#method.birth)

`Era::birth`[§](https://docs.rs#transaction-validity)Transaction Validity

The extension affects `longevity` of the transaction according to the [ Era](https://docs.rs/sp-runtime/48.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sp_runtime/generic/era/enum.Era.html) definition.

# CheckGenesis in frame_system - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/frame-system/48.0.0/frame_system/struct.CheckGenesis.html

## Expand description

Genesis hash check to provide replay protection between different networks.

[§](https://docs.rs#transaction-validity)Transaction Validity

Note that while a transaction with invalid `genesis_hash` will fail to be decoded,
the extension does not affect any other fields of `TransactionValidity` directly.

### impl<T: [Config](https://docs.rs/pallet/trait.Config.html) + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html)> [TransactionExtension](https://docs.rs/sp-runtime/48.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sp_runtime/traits/transaction_extension/trait.TransactionExtension.html)<<T as [Config](https://docs.rs/pallet/trait.Config.html)>::[RuntimeCall](https://docs.rs/pallet/trait.Config.html#associatedtype.RuntimeCall)> for [CheckGenesis](https://docs.rs/struct.CheckGenesis.html)<T>

Any additional data which was known at the time of transaction construction and can be
useful in authenticating the transaction. This is determined dynamically in part from the
on-chain environment using the

`implicit` function and not directly contained in the
transaction itself and therefore is considered “implicit”.The type that encodes information that can be passed from

`prepare` to `post_dispatch`.Determine any additional data which was known at the time of transaction construction and
can be useful in authenticating the transaction. The expected usage of this is to include in
any data which is signed and verified as part of transaction validation. Also perform any
pre-signature-verification checks and return an error if needed.

Do everything which would be done in a

[dispatch_transaction](https://docs.rs/sp-runtime/48.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sp_runtime/traits/transaction_extension/dispatch_transaction/trait.DispatchTransaction.html#tymethod.dispatch_transaction), but instead of executing the call, execute`substitute` instead. Since this doesn’t actually
dispatch the call, it doesn’t need to consume it and so `call` can be passed as a reference.[Source](https://docs.rs/parity-scale-codec/3.7.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/parity_scale_codec/codec.rs.html#379)

# frame_system::pallet - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/frame-system/48.0.0/frame_system/pallet/index.html

## Expand description

The `pallet` module in each FRAME pallet hosts the most important items needed
to construct this pallet.

The main components of this pallet are:

- `Pallet`- The subset of the functions that are dispatchable can be identified either in the
`dispatchables``Call`

- The subset of the functions that are dispatchable can be identified either in the
- `storage_types`- *Type Definitions*
- `Config`
- `Event`- `Error`- *Enums*

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [config_](https://docs.rs/config_preludes/index.html)- preludes
- Default implementations of `DefaultConfig``Config`
- [dispatchables](https://docs.rs/dispatchables/index.html)
- Auto-generated docs-only module listing all defined dispatchables for this pallet.
- [storage_](https://docs.rs/storage_types/index.html)- types
- Auto-generated docs-only module listing all (public and private) defined storage types for this pallet.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Genesis](https://docs.rs/struct.GenesisConfig.html)- Config
- Can be used to configure the
[genesis state](https://docs.substrate.io/build/genesis-configuration/)of this pallet.
- [Pallet](https://docs.rs/struct.Pallet.html)
- The `Pallet`struct, the main type that implements traits and standalone functions within the pallet.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Call](https://docs.rs/enum.Call.html)
- Contains a variant per dispatchable extrinsic that this pallet has.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Error for the System pallet
- [Event](https://docs.rs/enum.Event.html)
- Event for the System pallet.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Config](https://docs.rs/trait.Config.html)
- Configuration trait of this pallet.
- [Default](https://docs.rs/trait.DefaultConfig.html)- Config
- Based on `Config``#[pallet::config(with_default)]``#[register_default_config]``#[derive_impl]`

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Account](https://docs.rs/type.Account.html)
- The full account information for a particular account ID.
- [Block](https://docs.rs/type.BlockHash.html)- Hash
- Map of block numbers to block hashes.
- [Block](https://docs.rs/type.BlockSize.html)- Size
- Total size (in bytes) of the current block.
- [Block](https://docs.rs/type.BlockWeight.html)- Weight
- The current weight for the block.

- The weight reclaimed for the extrinsic.

- Whether all inherents have been applied.

- Stores the `spec_version`and`spec_name`of when the last runtime upgrade happened.

# frame_system::limits - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/frame-system/48.0.0/frame_system/limits/index.html

## Expand description

Block resource limits configuration structures.

FRAME defines two resources that are limited within a block:

- Weight (execution cost/time)
- Length (block size)

`frame_system` tracks consumption of each of these resources separately for each
`DispatchClass`. This module contains configuration object for both resources,
which should be passed to `frame_system` configuration when runtime is being set up.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Block](https://docs.rs/struct.BlockLength.html)- Length
- Block length limit configuration.
- [Block](https://docs.rs/struct.BlockLengthBuilder.html)- Length - Builder
- Builder for `BlockLength`
- [Block](https://docs.rs/struct.BlockWeights.html)- Weights
- Block weight limits & base values configuration.
- [Block](https://docs.rs/struct.BlockWeightsBuilder.html)- Weights - Builder
- An opinionated builder for `Weights`object.
- [Validation](https://docs.rs/struct.ValidationErrors.html)- Errors
- [Weights](https://docs.rs/struct.WeightsPerClass.html)- PerClass
- `DispatchClass`-specific weight configuration.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Validation](https://docs.rs/type.ValidationResult.html)- Result
- A result of validating `BlockWeights`correctness.

# frame_system::offchain - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/frame-system/48.0.0/frame_system/offchain/index.html

## Expand description

Module helpers for off-chain calls.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

This module provides transaction related helpers to:

- Submit a raw unsigned transaction
- Submit an unsigned transaction with a signed payload
- Submit a signed transaction.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Please refer to [ example-offchain-worker](https://docs.rs/pallet_example_offchain_worker/index.html) for
a concrete example usage of this crate.

[§](https://docs.rs#submit-a-raw-unsigned-transaction)Submit a raw unsigned transaction

To submit a raw unsigned transaction, [ SubmitTransaction](https://docs.rs/struct.SubmitTransaction.html)
can be used.

[§](https://docs.rs#signing-transactions)Signing transactions

To be able to use signing, the following trait should be implemented:

- `AppCrypto`
- `CreateSignedTransaction`

[§](https://docs.rs#submit-an-unsigned-transaction-with-a-signed-payload)Submit an unsigned transaction with a signed payload

Initially, a payload instance that implements the `SignedPayload` trait should be defined.
See `PricePayload`

The payload type that is defined defined can then be signed and submitted onchain.

[§](https://docs.rs#submit-a-signed-transaction)Submit a signed transaction

[ Signer](https://docs.rs/struct.Signer.html) can be used to sign/verify payloads

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Account](https://docs.rs/struct.Account.html)
- Details of an account for which a private key is contained in the keystore.
- [ForAll](https://docs.rs/struct.ForAll.html)
- Marker struct used to flag using all supported keys to sign a payload.
- [ForAny](https://docs.rs/struct.ForAny.html)
- Marker struct used to flag using any of the supported keys to sign a payload.
- [Signer](https://docs.rs/struct.Signer.html)
- Provides an implementation for signing transaction payloads.
- [Submit](https://docs.rs/struct.SubmitTransaction.html)- Transaction
- Provides the ability to directly submit signed and unsigned transaction onchain.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [AppCrypto](https://docs.rs/trait.AppCrypto.html)
- A type binding runtime-level `Public/Signature`pair with crypto wrapped by`RuntimeAppPublic`.
- [Create](https://docs.rs/trait.CreateAuthorizedTransaction.html)- Authorized - Transaction
- Interface for creating a transaction for a call that will be authorized.
- [Create](https://docs.rs/trait.CreateBare.html)- Bare
- Interface for creating a bare extrinsic.
- [Create](https://docs.rs/trait.CreateInherent.html)- Inherent
- Interface for creating an inherent; ⚠️  **Deprecated use**.`CreateBare`
- [Create](https://docs.rs/trait.CreateSignedTransaction.html)- Signed - Transaction
- Interface for creating an old-school signed transaction.
- [Create](https://docs.rs/trait.CreateTransaction.html)- Transaction
- Interface for creating a transaction.
- [Create](https://docs.rs/trait.CreateTransactionBase.html)- Transaction - Base
- Common interface for the `CreateTransaction`trait family to unify the`Call`type.
- [Send](https://docs.rs/trait.SendSignedTransaction.html)- Signed - Transaction
- Submit a signed transaction to the transaction pool.
- [Send](https://docs.rs/trait.SendUnsignedTransaction.html)- Unsigned - Transaction
- Submit an unsigned transaction onchain with a signed payload
- [Sign](https://docs.rs/trait.SignMessage.html)- Message
- A message signer.
- [Signed](https://docs.rs/trait.SignedPayload.html)- Payload
- Utility trait to be implemented on payloads that can be signed.
- [Signing](https://docs.rs/trait.SigningTypes.html)- Types
- A wrapper around the types which are used for signing.

Information of an account.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.nonce)

`nonce: Nonce`The number of transactions this account has sent.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.consumers)

`consumers: `[RefCount](https://docs.rs/type.RefCount.html)The number of other modules that currently depend on this account’s existence. The account cannot be reaped until this is zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.providers)

`providers: `[RefCount](https://docs.rs/type.RefCount.html)The number of other modules that allow this account to exist. The account may not be reaped
until this and `sufficients` are both zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.sufficients)

`sufficients: `[RefCount](https://docs.rs/type.RefCount.html)The number of modules that allow this account to exist for their own purposes only. The
account may not be reaped until this and `providers` are both zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.data)

`data: AccountData`The additional data that belongs to this account. Used to store the balance(s) in a lot of chains.
